watchlist.thesis: Palantir remains one of the strongest liquid software setups, with StockLens scoring it 71 and its technical domain bullish despite a bearish macro backdrop.
CrowdStrike has a strongly bullish StockLens technical score of 87 and remains a relative-strength leader, but its risk and macro scores argue for buying controlled pullbacks rather than chasing.
Palo Alto Networks retains bullish technical structure and is a liquid cybersecurity leader, although weak fundamental, risk and macro scores make entries more selective.
Fortinet remains a liquid cybersecurity momentum candidate with its October 28 event as the main near-term risk, favoring a post-earnings setup.
Microsoft remains a core liquid cloud and AI leader, but its confirmed October 28 earnings release makes any pre-event swing inherently gap-sensitive.
Apple offers deep liquidity and a durable mega-cap trend, while its confirmed November 2 earnings date makes event-aware position sizing essential.
Salesforce remains a liquid software candidate for orderly pullbacks as investors rotate selectively within technology rather than abandoning the sector wholesale.
ServiceNow remains a high-liquidity cloud-software trend candidate, but the broader AI/software volatility favors confirmation after consolidation.
Cloudflare remains a high-beta software momentum name with strong liquidity, best approached after volatility contracts rather than after a sharp upside burst.
Datadog remains a liquid cloud-observability momentum candidate as software leadership broadens selectively beyond the largest AI names.
Veeva provides liquid healthcare-software exposure with a cleaner diversification angle while technology leadership remains uneven.
Texas Instruments is a liquid semiconductor leader worth monitoring for relative-strength confirmation while the broader chip group remains volatile.
Exxon has a strongly bullish StockLens technical score of 86 and is trading at a reported 52-week high, making it a leading liquid energy momentum candidate ahead of October 30 results.
Chevron remains a high-liquidity energy trend candidate as XLE trades near a new 52-week high, but oil-price volatility and earnings timing require event-aware entries.
ConocoPhillips offers liquid upstream energy exposure aligned with current sector leadership, with crude-price reversals the principal momentum risk.
EOG is a liquid exploration-and-production candidate benefiting from the energy leadership regime while retaining sensitivity to oil-price headlines.
Occidental offers higher-beta liquid energy exposure suited to momentum swings, but the trade should be sized for commodity and geopolitical volatility.
Cheniere provides liquid LNG exposure in the strongest current sector theme, with the October 29 earnings event making post-report confirmation preferable.
Marathon Petroleum is a liquid refining momentum candidate benefiting from strong energy-sector breadth while remaining sensitive to crack spreads and crude volatility.
GE Vernova offers liquid power-infrastructure exposure to the AI electricity-buildout theme, but its valuation and macro sensitivity argue for disciplined breakout confirmation.

sector_notes: The latest live FactIQ snapshot shows SPY up 0.50%, QQQ up 0.42%, XLE up 0.48% and SMH up 1.15% on October 26, so the session is recovering even though the recent tape has been volatile. Energy remains the clearest structural leader, with XLE at 69.66 against a reported 52-week high of 69.855, while semiconductors are bouncing but remain exposed to the AI-spending debate. Brent crude has eased from six-month highs and US futures are modestly higher ahead of a week containing roughly one-third of S&P 500 earnings and an expected October Fed hold, keeping event risk elevated. StockLens shows a sharp split inside software: PLTR is rated Solid with a 79 technical score, CRWD has an 87 technical score but strongly bearish macro conditions, and PANW has bullish technicals but weak fundamentals and risk scores, so selectivity remains more important than sector-level exposure.

earnings_flags.note: Cadence is scheduled to report after the close today; treat the session as an earnings-event day and avoid opening a fresh swing immediately before the release.
Visa has officially confirmed fiscal Q4 and full-year 2026 results after the close on October 27, creating material payment-spending and guidance gap risk.
Microsoft officially confirms FY27 Q1 results after the close on October 28; cloud growth, AI capex and margins are major gap drivers.
Alphabet is scheduled to report Q3 results on October 28; advertising, cloud growth and AI spending create large-cap gap risk even though GOOGL is not currently on the long watchlist.
Fortinet officially confirms its Q3 2026 earnings event for October 28 at 4:30 p.m. ET, making cybersecurity guidance the immediate gap-risk catalyst.
Amazon is scheduled to report Q3 results on October 29; AWS growth, margins and AI infrastructure spending are major gap-risk variables.
Eli Lilly officially confirms its Q3 2026 earnings call for October 29; product demand, guidance and pipeline updates can generate a material gap.
Cheniere is listed for an October 29 earnings event; verify the final release timing before carrying a swing position through the report.
ExxonMobil officially confirms Q3 2026 results for October 30 at 5:30 a.m. CT with an 8:30 a.m. CT call, making oil prices and production guidance key gap drivers.
Apple officially confirms its FY26 fourth-quarter results conference call for November 2 at 5:00 p.m. ET, creating significant mega-cap event risk.
AMD is a large-cap semiconductor name with an upcoming November 3 results event; AI demand, data-center guidance and chip-sector sentiment can amplify the gap.

avoid.reason: The semiconductor complex remains vulnerable to renewed AI-spending concerns, so require clear relative-strength confirmation before treating Nvidia as a fresh momentum long.
Broad AI-infrastructure sentiment is still being tested by financing and return-on-capex concerns, making a confirmed trend continuation preferable to anticipation.
AMD has an imminent earnings catalyst and high sensitivity to semiconductor and AI expectations, so event risk overwhelms the benefit of initiating a new swing before confirmation.
Marvell remains highly sensitive to the same AI-infrastructure spending concerns that have recently driven sharp moves across semiconductor names.
Applied Materials remains exposed to semiconductor-cycle volatility and lacks enough evidence in this pass to rank above the stronger liquid setups.
KLA is exposed to the current semiconductor volatility regime and is better treated as a post-sector-confirmation candidate than a pre-breakout chase.
Lam Research remains tightly coupled to semiconductor-capex sentiment, so wait for sustained relative strength rather than anticipating a sector reversal.
Intel combines semiconductor volatility with near-term earnings risk, making the risk-adjusted setup inferior to cleaner momentum names.
Alphabet has major earnings risk on October 28 and the current AI-spending debate makes an event-driven position less attractive than waiting for the report.
Meta's recently raised AI-infrastructure spending plans have increased investor sensitivity to capital intensity and financing, making the risk/reward less clean ahead of the broader earnings wave.
CoreWeave has been among the hardest-hit AI-infrastructure names amid debt and financing concerns, so its volatility is too high for the clean momentum profile sought here.
